questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects the permissions database when a popular cache entry is missing or expires? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A single API instance receives 300 concurrent requests for the same user whose entry is not cached anywhere. How many database loads does that instance start for this key?
choices: 300, because every request runs its own factory delegate before the cache is populated
One for the in-flight load; the other callers wait on the same result
Zero, because Redis is always consulted first and it always has the value
Two: one for the local cache layer and one for the distributed layer

questions.prompt: An administrator revokes a role, the transaction commits, and GrantChangedHandler runs on instance A. How fresh is the permission data on instance B?
choices: Immediately fresh, because RemoveAsync on A clears every instance's memory
Fresh as soon as Redis is cleared, because HybridCache keeps no copy in process memory
Possibly stale for up to the 45 second local expiry, since B may still hold its in-process copy
Stale for the full 10 minute Expiration, because removal does not affect the distributed cache

questions.prompt: The database stalls and LoadAsync exceeds its 3 second budget while many requests wait on that load. What is the outcome?
choices: The waiting callers receive an OperationCanceledException, nothing is cached, and the next request starts a new load
The cache stores an empty EffectivePermissions so callers are denied quickly until expiry
The factory keeps running without a limit because the timeout only applies to the first caller
The callers receive the previous value, since HybridCache always serves stale data on failure
